rewrites.title: Lineage-tracked inheritance of the primed state through division and passaging
rewrites.description: Prime cells with an AP-1 stimulus, then serially passage them with strong dilution, using barcoded lineages, single-cell multiome (RNA and ATAC) and live AP-1 reporters. Test whether the primed state persists, is heritable by clone, and re-establishes after dilution without the stimulus, and whether passing it on requires continued AP-1 binding (acute degron versus no degron). Persistence through repeated dilution would indicate a self-propagating state.

rewrites.title: Persistence of AP-1 binding and accessibility after stimulus withdrawal
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TNF, serum, or a stress signal) and then withdraw it. Measure AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy by CUT&RUN and chromatin accessibility by ATAC-seq days to weeks later. If AP-1 sites stay open and bound after the signal is gone, that supports AP-1 as a memory mechanism.

rewrites.title: Single-cell AP-1 fluctuation statistics as predictors of memory
rewrites.description: Live-image an endogenous FOS/JUN reporter (MS2 or knock-in fluorescent tag) in single cells over days and measure the autocorrelation and pulse statistics of AP-1 activity. Test whether cells with higher pulse frequency or longer autocorrelation show a primed response (faster, stronger re-induction of target genes) on restimulation. Then use optogenetic control to deliver the same total dose as bursts or as a plateau, to test causally whether the temporal pattern encodes memory.

rewrites.title: Long-term chromatin accessibility tracking after a transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or keratinocytes) to a defined pulse of an AP-1-activating stimulus such as TPA, wounding cytokines, or inflammatory signals. After withdrawal, run time-course ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for Fos/Jun, and H3K27ac profiling to see whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist for days to weeks after AP-1 activity returns to baseline.

rewrites.title: Single-site versus combinatorial AP-1 motif disruption
rewrites.description: Test whether memory depends on multiple overlapping, partially redundant AP-1 sites rather than any single enhancer. Use CRISPR base-editing of AP-1 motifs singly and in combinations at stimulus-primed loci, then measure the decay time of the enhanced re-response after stimulus withdrawal, to see whether persistence scales with the number of intact sites instead of depending on any one.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or stress), wash out, then re-challenge after days to weeks. Compare transcriptional output and AP-1 occupancy with naive cells to test whether a persistent, stimulus-independent change in responsiveness exists.

rewrites.title: Acute degron depletion to separate establishment from maintenance
rewrites.description: Use auxin- or dTAG-inducible degradation of FOS/JUN family members before, during, and after the priming stimulus. If depletion only during priming erases later hyper-responsiveness but depletion after priming does not, AP-1 is needed for establishing memory; if post-priming depletion also erases it, AP-1 is needed for maintenance.

rewrites.title: Mapping AP-1-bound latent enhancers by ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN
rewrites.description: Profile AP-1 binding (JUN/FOS CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility, and H3K27ac before, after, and long after stimulus withdrawal. Identify enhancers that stay open or primed after AP-1 levels return to baseline, and test whether they are the sites that drive faster or stronger reactivation.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 recruitment sufficiency test
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based recruitment of FOS/JUN, or insert AP-1 motifs, at a naive locus, with and without pioneer factor co-binding. Test whether transient AP-1 occupancy alone creates persistent accessibility, histone marks (H3K27ac/H3K4me1), and faster re-induction, and whether motif mutations at endogenous memory enhancers abolish these effects.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell reporters of AP-1 dynamics
rewrites.description: Use paired scRNA/scATAC-seq and live imaging of AP-1 activity reporters (e.g., FOS-GFP knock-in, AP-1 motif reporters) to track whether individual cells retain heritable AP-1-linked accessibility states through divisions. Lineage tracing or sister-cell comparisons would distinguish cell-autonomous, mitotically heritable memory from population-level selection or persistent paracrine signaling.

rewrites.title: Time course of accessibility after transient stimulus and washout
rewrites.description: Give cells a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA or a cytokine), wash it out, and run ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at several times from hours to weeks. This tests whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist after the signal is gone and AP-1 levels have fallen.

rewrites.title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter with optogenetic pulse patterning
rewrites.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or an AP-1 transcriptional reporter while delivering controlled optogenetic or ERK-pulse inputs of varying duration, frequency, and rest interval. Fit input-history-dependent response curves (hysteresis, paired-pulse enhancement) to determine whether the system integrates past dynamics and for how long, giving quantitative memory timescales.

rewrites.title: Stimulus-order permutation with chromatin readout
rewrites.description: Expose cells to many different orderings of the same pulses (e.g., TNF, EGF, stress, or phorbol ester), with each ordering differing from another by a change in only one adjacent step. Then measure ATAC-seq accessibility at AP-1 (FOS/JUN) motif sites and the transcriptional response to a common test challenge. If the response depends on order and not just total dose, AP-1 acts as a history-dependent memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and reporters across lineages
rewrites.description: Track endogenous FOS/JUN with fluorescent knock-ins and AP-1 target reporters over many days in single cells and their lineages, to ask whether past activity history predicts later response and whether states are inherited through division. Lineage-correlation and mother–daughter analyses separate cell-autonomous heritable memory from persistent external signaling.

rewrites.title: Synthetic sufficiency test with optogenetic or CRISPR-targeted AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Pulse AP-1 activity with optogenetic FOS/JUN, or use dCas9-based recruitment or deletion of specific AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers. Then measure whether accessibility, pioneer-factor cooperation (e.g., with BAF), and gene responsiveness persist after the pulse, testing sufficiency and locus-specific necessity.

rewrites.title: Site-specific perturbation of memory enhancers and cooperating factors
rewrites.description: Use CRISPRi/dCas9 or motif mutation at candidate AP-1-dependent memory enhancers, and pioneer-factor or chromatin-remodeler (e.g., BAF) loss, to test whether the sites are necessary for faster re-induction of nearby genes. Pair this with Hi-C or Micro-C and histone-mark profiling to determine whether AP-1 maintains memory directly or by recruiting other chromatin regulators.

rewrites.title: Chromatin accessibility memory readout after transient stimulus (ATAC/CUT&Tag)
rewrites.description: Give cells a brief inflammatory or injury stimulus (e.g., TNF or wounding), wash it out, and profile AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and chromatin accessibility by CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq at days 0, 1, 7 and 28. Compare AP-1 motif sites in primed cells with those in naive cells to test whether they remain persistently open after stimulation.

rewrites.title: Motif mutation and dose titration at single enhancers to test threshold behavior
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR base-editing of single AP-1 motifs (partial versus full disruption) and titrate stimulus dose and duration. Measure the effect on persistent accessibility and re-stimulation response to find threshold-like (nonlinear) behavior, which would indicate AP-1 sites act as discrete memory switches.

rewrites.title: Targeted epigenome editing and sufficiency tests at AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Use dCas9 to recruit or block AP-1 at specific primed enhancers, or mutate the motifs, with CRISPRi/a and base editing. Then test whether deposited marks and the primed response last without the original stimulus. Pair this with Hi-C or Micro-C to see whether AP-1-dependent enhancer–promoter contacts carry the memory, testing whether AP-1 binding is necessary and sufficient and not merely correlated.

rewrites.title: Sufficiency by site-specific addition and removal of AP-1 motifs or recruitment
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based tools to add or remove AP-1 motifs or AP-1 recruitment at chosen enhancers (e.g., motif deletion by base editing, or dCas9-FOS recruitment) in naive and primed cells. Test whether deleting motifs erases the faster or stronger re-response at that locus, and whether artificially recruiting AP-1 to a naive locus is enough to install a memory-like response without the original stimulus.
